target: UTM-bundled QEMU, HVF, one vCPU, VirtIO keyboard/tablet and WAV-backed virtio-sound-pci
command: QEMU=build/utm-qemu-probe/qemu-probe QEMU_VIRT='-L /Applications/UTM.app/Contents/Resources/qemu -machine virt,accel=hvf,gic-version=3 -cpu host -smp 1 -m 1024 -device virtio-ramfb -device virtio-keyboard-device -device virtio-tablet-device -audiodev wav,id=sound0,path=build/psalmody-current-audio-2026-11-12.wav -device virtio-sound-pci,audiodev=sound0' ZEAL_COMPAT_LOG_PATH=build/check-psalmody-current-audio-2026-11-12.log python3 -u scripts/check-compat.py --pci --quick --probe-psalmody --probe-psalmody-audio-timer
verified: Psalmody launched through the graphical terminal, accepted note input, played the note, exited with Shift+Escape, and returned to a working terminal.
The WAV-backed VirtIO sound device captured 18,522 stereo frames at 44,100 Hz; 29,988 samples were nonzero, with peak amplitude 7,000 and RMS about 6,252.
The strongest sustained tone measured about 523.5 Hz, consistent with C5.
The experimental sound timer delivered 22 IRQs.
After exit, the terminal evaluated 40+2 as 42 and zstatus reported failed=0.
scope_note: This verifies app interaction and generated PCM under UTM-bundled QEMU with a WAV sink. It does not replace live audible-output acceptance, which the user has separately confirmed for UTM and Pi HDMI/headphone output.
